title: Chronological Query Language (CQL)
text: Used simple way , stratigraphr’s CQL interface offers little benefit writing CQL directly. real power combining cql() R tools build models based data. following examples, use simple example dataset radiocarbon dates:
code: library("purrr") library("dplyr") #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  dates <- data.frame(   lab_id = c("ABC-001", "ABC-002", "ABC-003", "ABC-004", "ABC-005"),   age = c(5050, 5000, 4950, 4900, 4850),   error = c(30, 30, 30, 30, 30),   phase = c("Phase 1", "Phase 1", "Phase 1", "Phase 2", "Phase 2") )

title: Chronological Query Language (CQL)
text: radiocarbon data tabular format, can take advantage dplyr’s powerful tools data manipulation build CQL models programmatically. example, use dplyr::mutate() concisely express table dates CQL R_Date commands: use dplyr::group_by() dplyr::summarise() build phase models. three stage process: Preprocess dates, e.g. order phases. Group dates phase summarise cql_phase(). Group phases sequence, using boundaries automatically add boundary constraints .
code: dates |>   mutate(r_date = cql_r_date(lab_id, age, error)) |>   pluck("r_date") |>   cql() #>  // CQL2 generated by stratigraphr v0.4.0.9000 #>  R_Date("ABC-001", 5050, 30); #>  R_Date("ABC-002", 5000, 30); #>  R_Date("ABC-003", 4950, 30); #>  R_Date("ABC-004", 4900, 30); #>  R_Date("ABC-005", 4850, 30); dates |>   group_by(phase) |>   summarise(cql = cql_phase(phase, cql_r_date(lab_id, age, error))) |>   arrange(desc(phase)) |>   summarise(cql = cql_sequence("Example Sequence", cql, boundaries = TRUE)) |>   pluck("cql") |>   cql() ->   example_cql  example_cql #>  // CQL2 generated by stratigraphr v0.4.0.9000 #>  Sequence("Example Sequence") #>  { #>   Boundary(""); #>   Phase("Phase 2") #>   { #>    R_Date("ABC-004", 4900, 30); #>    R_Date("ABC-005", 4850, 30); #>   }; #>   Boundary(""); #>   Phase("Phase 1") #>   { #>    R_Date("ABC-001", 5050, 30); #>    R_Date("ABC-002", 5000, 30); #>    R_Date("ABC-003", 4950, 30); #>   }; #>   Boundary(""); #>  };

text: can run models generated cql() using desktop online versions OxCal simply copying output program. Alternatively, use write_oxcal() create .oxcal file: can also run OxCal directly R using oxcAAR package. depends local installation OxCal. already one installed, can set path executable using oxcAAR::setOxcalExecutablePath(). Otherwise, use oxcAAR::quickSetupOxcal() download one, example temporary directory: can use oxcAAR::executeOxcalScript() run CQL script oxcAAR::readOxcalOutput() read output back R. can parse output oxcAAR::parseOxcalOutput() visualise using oxcAAR’s built-plotting functions:  current CRAN version oxcAAR (v. 1.0.0) read posterior probabilities produced model Bayesian calibration, work need install latest development version (devtools::install_github("ISAAKiel/oxcAAR")). , oxcAAR::parseOxcalOutput() also contains modelled results $posterior_sigma_ranges $posterior_probabilities. , can quickly visualise built-plotting functions:
code: oxcal_cql <- cql(   cql_r_date("ABC-001", 9100, 30),   cql_r_date("ABC-002", 9200, 30),   cql_r_date("ABC-003", 9300, 30) )  write_oxcal(oxcal_cql, "cql.oxcal") library("oxcAAR") quickSetupOxcal(path = tempdir()) executeOxcalScript(oxcal_cql) |>   readOxcalOutput() ->   oxcal_output oxcal_parsed <- oxcAAR::parseOxcalOutput(oxcal_output) plot(oxcal_parsed) calcurve_plot(oxcal_parsed) # Not run: slow example_oxcal <- executeOxcalScript(example_cql) readOxcalOutput(example_oxcal) |>   parseOxcalOutput() |>   plot()

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: Archaeological stratigraphy records depositional history site set units1 relative temporal ordering determining law superposition (Harris 1979). stratigraphic graph formal representation information: directed acyclic graph nodes represent units directed edges represent stratigraphic relations (Dye Buck 2015). Harris matrix conventional visual representation stratigraphic graph, units arranged boxes lines indicate direct stratigraphic relations (Harris 1979). terms sometimes used interchangeably archaeological literature, useful distinguish abstract data structure (stratigraphic graph) visual representation (Harris matrix). information commonly featured Harris matrices – unit equivalencies, distinction deposits interfaces, unit types, phase assignments – part pure stratigraphic graph. associated information can used display, analysis, modelling, graph structure determined solely /relations units.

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: stratigraph object package’s central data structure. specialised subclass tidygraph::tbl_graph, representing stratigraphic graph tidy data nodes (units) edges (relations). package includes dataset harris12, classic stratigraphic sequence Harris (1979, fig. 12): data frame contains context column unit labels list-columns (, , equal) describing stratigraphic relations units. construct graph, specify column contains unit labels column describes relations: direction argument (default "") indicates whether relation column lists units unit. stratigraph inherits tbl_graph, can manipulated using full suite tidygraph igraph functions: See tidygraph documentation details tidy graph manipulation analysis.
code: library("stratigraphr")  data("harris12") harris12 #>    context   above   below equal #> 1        1      NA 2, 3, 4  <NA> #> 2        2       1       5  <NA> #> 3        3       1       5  <NA> #> 4        4       1       5  <NA> #> 5        5 2, 3, 4       6  <NA> #> 6        6       5    7, 8  <NA> #> 7        7       6       9     8 #> 8        8       6       9     7 #> 9        9    7, 8 natural  <NA> #> 10 natural       9      NA  <NA> h12_graph <- stratigraph(harris12, "context", "above") h12_graph #> # A stratigraph: 10 units and 12 relations #> # ✔ Valid stratigraphic graph #>                 1 #> ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐ #> 2               3               4 #> └───────────────┼───────────────┘ #>                 5 #>                 │ #>                 6 #>         ┌───────┴───────┐ #>         7               8 #>         └───────┬───────┘ #>                 9 #>                 │ #>              natural library("tidygraph")  # Inspect the nodes (units) h12_graph |>   activate("nodes") |>   as_tibble() #> # A tibble: 10 × 4 #>    context above below     equal #>    <chr>   <chr> <list>    <chr> #>  1 1       NA    <chr [3]> NA    #>  2 2       1     <chr [1]> NA    #>  3 3       1     <chr [1]> NA    #>  4 4       1     <chr [1]> NA    #>  5 5       2     <chr [1]> NA    #>  6 6       5     <chr [2]> NA    #>  7 7       6     <chr [1]> 8     #>  8 8       6     <chr [1]> 7     #>  9 9       7     <chr [1]> NA    #> 10 natural 9     <chr [1]> NA  # Inspect the edges (relations) h12_graph |>   activate("edges") |>   as_tibble() #> # A tibble: 12 × 2 #>     from    to #>    <int> <int> #>  1     1     2 #>  2     1     3 #>  3     1     4 #>  4     2     5 #>  5     3     5 #>  6     4     5 #>  7     5     6 #>  8     6     7 #>  9     6     8 #> 10     7     9 #> 11     8     9 #> 12     9    10

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: Stratigraphic data fundamentally simple: data frame units relations. stratigraph() function expects: label column unique identifiers unit relation column describing stratigraphic relations units relation column can either list-column (element vector related units) regular column long format (row represents single relation).

title: Stratigraphic graphs

code: strat_data <- data.frame(   unit = c("A", "B", "C"),   below = c("B", "C", NA) )  stratigraph(strat_data, "unit", "below", direction = "below") #> # A stratigraph: 3 units and 2 relations #> # ✔ Valid stratigraphic graph #> A #> │ #> B #> │ #> C

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: commonly, stratigraphic data stored CSV file. long-format input, can read CSV pass directly stratigraph(): Stratigraphic data often includes ‘’ ‘’ columns. describe graph opposite perspectives. Use strat_is_mirror() verify consistent:
code: library("readr")  csv_text <- "context,above A, B,A C,A"  strat_data <- read_csv(csv_text, show_col_types = FALSE)  stratigraph(strat_data, "context", "above") #> # A stratigraph: 3 units and 2 relations #> # ✔ Valid stratigraphic graph #>   A #> ┌─┴─┐ #> B   C strat_is_mirror(harris12$context, harris12$above, harris12$below) #> [1] TRUE

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: Following Dye Buck (2015), valid stratigraphic graph2 must satisfy two properties: acyclic – contains cycles, .e. circular chains relations. cycle mean unit unit B, B C, C , violating law stratigraphic superposition. contains redundant relations – relation redundant already implied relations transitivity. Transitivity means B B C, necessarily C; direct relation C adds new information. Per Harris’ ‘Law Stratigraphical Succession’, uppermost undermost relations significant placing unit stratigraphic sequence. stratigraph() function warns construction graph invalid, allows create inspect invalid graphs. Use strg_is_valid() explicit checking:
code: strg_is_valid(h12_graph) #> [1] TRUE

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: cycle occurs stratigraphic relations contradictory. violates law superposition indicates error data:
code: cycle_data <- data.frame(   unit = c("A", "B", "C"),   below = c("B", "C", "A") )  cycle_graph <- stratigraph(cycle_data, "unit", "below", direction = "below")

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: redundant relation one already implied transitivity. example, B B C, ’s position C already established chain –B–C. explicit relation C redundant removed produce valid stratigraphic graph. strg_prune() function computes transitive reduction, removing redundant edges:
code: redundant_data <- data.frame(   unit = c("A", "B", "B", "C"),   above = c("B", "C", "C", NA) )  redundant_graph <- stratigraph(redundant_data, "unit", "above") strg_is_valid(redundant_graph) #> [1] FALSE pruned_graph <- strg_prune(redundant_graph) pruned_graph #> # A stratigraph: 3 units and 2 relations #> # ✔ Valid stratigraphic graph #> C #> │ #> B #> │ #> A strg_is_valid(pruned_graph) #> [1] TRUE

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: ggraph extends grammar graphics network visualisation, providing ggplot2-compatible interface plotting graph data. stratigraph objects inherit tbl_graph, work seamlessly ggraph: can map aesthetics, add layers, use geoms just tidy data. Harris matrix conventional visual representation stratigraphic graph. can reproduce using ggraph Sugiyama (layered) layout:  Sugiyama layout arranges units horizontal layers according stratigraphic position, earliest (lowest) units bottom. geom_edge_elbow() geom produces right-angled edges characteristic Harris matrices.
code: library("ggraph")  ggraph(h12_graph, layout = "sugiyama") +   geom_edge_elbow() +   geom_node_label(aes(label = context), label.r = unit(0, "mm")) +   theme_graph()

title: Stratigraphic graphs
text: stratigraphic graph contains units relations, can use associated information enhance visualisation. shub1 dataset (Richter et al. 2017) includes columns context type, phase, structure, can mapped visual aesthetics:
code: shub1_graph <- stratigraph(shub1, "context", "above")  ggraph(shub1_graph, layout = "sugiyama") +   geom_edge_elbow() +   geom_node_point(aes(shape = type), fill = "white", size = 6) +   geom_node_text(aes(label = context), vjust = 0.5, size = 3) +   scale_shape_manual(values = c(22, 21, 23, 24)) +   theme_graph()

title: Describe a boundary constraint in CQL — cql_boundary
text: CQL command Boundary describes constraints within ordered sequence (see cql_sequence()). Groups events two boundaries assumed sampled prior distribution. Boundary alone models uniform prior. types boundary, .e. Sigma_Boundary, Tau_Boundary, Zero_Boundary yet implemented stratigraphr. Boundaries can contain Transition command, case describe non-instantaneous transition 'trapezium' prior.

code: # Uniform model with unknown boundaries cql(   cql_boundary("P1 start"),   cql_phase("P1", list(     cql_r_date("A", 5050, 30),     cql_r_date("B", 5000, 30),     cql_r_date("C", 4950, 30)   )),   cql_boundary("P1 end") ) #>  // CQL2 generated by stratigraphr v0.4.0.9000 #>  Boundary("P1 start"); #>  Phase("P1") #>  { #>   R_Date("A", 5050, 30); #>   R_Date("B", 5000, 30); #>   R_Date("C", 4950, 30); #>  }; #>  Boundary("P1 end");  # Uniform model with boundaries with a prior likelihood cql(   cql_boundary("P1 start",                prior = cql_date("P1S-Prior", cql_u("", 5200, 5100))),   cql_phase("P1", list(     cql_r_date("A", 5050, 30),     cql_r_date("B", 5000, 30),     cql_r_date("C", 4950, 30)   )),   cql_boundary("P1 end",                prior = cql_date("P1E-Prior", cql_u("", 4800, 4900))) ) #>  // CQL2 generated by stratigraphr v0.4.0.9000 #>  Boundary("P1 start", Date("P1S-Prior", U("", 5200, 5100));); #>  Phase("P1") #>  { #>   R_Date("A", 5050, 30); #>   R_Date("B", 5000, 30); #>   R_Date("C", 4950, 30); #>  }; #>  Boundary("P1 end", Date("P1E-Prior", U("", 4800, 4900)););  # 'Trapezium' model cql(   cql_boundary("P1 start",     cql_transition("")   ),   cql_phase("P1", list(     cql_r_date("A", 5050, 30),     cql_r_date("B", 5000, 30),     cql_r_date("C", 4950, 30)   )),   cql_boundary("P1 end",     cql_transition("")   ) ) #>  // CQL2 generated by stratigraphr v0.4.0.9000 #>  Boundary("P1 start") #>  { #>   Transition(""); #>  }; #>  Phase("P1") #>  { #>   R_Date("A", 5050, 30); #>   R_Date("B", 5000, 30); #>   R_Date("C", 4950, 30); #>  }; #>  Boundary("P1 end") #>  { #>   Transition(""); #>  };

title: Describe distributions in CQL — cql_n
text: CQL commands N, LnN, T, U Top_Hat describe various types probability distribution functions. cql_n() defines normal distribution mean standard deviation; cql_lnn() log–normal distribution mean standard deviation; cql_t() Student's t distribution degrees freedom; cql_u() uniform distribution start end; cql_top_hat() uniform distribution central point width.

title: Set OxCal options in CQL — cql_options
text: bcad Logical. Whether BC/AD used log file output. convergence_data Logical. Whether sample convergence data included output data file. curve Character. default calibration curve. cubic Logical. Whether cubic (opposed linear) interpolation used calibration curves. ensembles Integer. number age-depth ensembles stored analysis. floruit Logical. Whether quantile ranges calculated instead default highest posterior density (hpd). intercept Logical. Whether intercept method used radiocarbon calibration ranges. k_iterations Integer. default number MCMC passes. plus_minus Logical. Whether + - used place BC AD log files. raw_data Logical. Whether raw calibration curve data included output data file. resolution Integer. default bin size probability distributions Date Interval type. round Logical. Whether ranges rounded . round_by Integer. Resolution rounding (0 automatic). sd1 Logical. Whether 68.2% (1 σ) ranges given log tab delimited files. sd2 Logical. Whether 95.4% (2 σ) ranges given log tab delimited files. sd3 Logical. Whether 99.7% (3 σ) ranges given log tab delimited files. uniform_span_prior Logical. Whether two extra prior factors suggested Nicholls Jones 2001 used. use_f14c Logical. Whether calibrations take place F14C space (rather BP space). year Numeric. datum point ages - default mid AD 1950. ... Additional named arguments converted OxCal options. See details.

title: stratigraphr (development version)
text: stratigraph() supports tidy/long-format data frames row represents single relation (#15) Validation now considers redundant relations. strat_is_valid() renamed strg_is_valid() (#21) silently returns logical value. Use strg_validate() raise error invalid stratigraphs strg_validate(warn = TRUE) raise warning. Adds print() method stratigraphs including validations status Minimum supported R version now 4.1 Removes shub1_radiocarbon dataset (also now found c14) Adds dependencies vctrs vroom Drops dependencies rcarbon, magrittr, tidyr, Bchron (suggested) ggplot2 (suggested) Downgrades dependencies tibble, dplyr readr suggested

title: stratigraphr 0.3.0
text: New S3 object cal, generic representation calibrated probability distributions Methods printing summarising cal objects Type conversion functions cal objects (as_cal.CalDates(), as_cal.oxcAARCalibratedDatesList() as_cal.BchronCalibratedDates()) New vignette("tidy_radiocarbon") Breaking change: cal() sum() renamed c14_calibrate c14_sum now return cal objects. Renamed functions: harris() → strat_connect(), is_valid_harris() → strat_is_valid() Removed notion “type” stratigraph(). stratigraph() now return graph even stratigraphically valid. Renamed vignette("harris") → vignette("stratigraph") Utility functions validating stratigraphies: strat_is_mirror() Fixed read_lst() reading Stratify ‘extended’ LST files Added NEWS.md file track changes package.
